jobs.prompt: Write a change order to the Project Swarm roadmap scope: a new stage S10 Swarm Watch Command Center, an UPGRADE of Swarm Watch, not a replacement. Files: (1) edit docs/scope/roadmap.md: add the line "- S10: Swarm Watch Command Center (Hive overview, project cockpit, command palette, tools hub)" after the S9 line in the Stages list and append a new section "## S10 Swarm Watch Command Center" at the end with requirements R-066 to R-080 in exactly the style of the existing sections (### R-0NN Sentence. then Acceptance: with 3 to 5 checkable bullets: a command, a number, a file, an exit code or a visible result). Do not change any existing text. (2) create docs/architecture/command-center.md (under 400 lines): goal; what stays (every current view and route stays and moves under a Classic tab, nothing removed); View 1 The Hive; View 2 Project Cockpit; experience (guided tour, command palette, Resources and Tools hub, phone layout); the signature glitch style; data rules (real data only, one source per number, labelled, hover explanation, a number that cannot be accurate is not shown); performance and accessibility rules; asset policy; the self-review loop; stages CC1 to CC5 each with a gate; risks; what is deliberately not built; an originality statement: the entity and layout are our own design, the owner described two reference posts as inspiration only, no art, characters or text from them are copied. (3) create docs/design/review-rubric.md: the rubric table, 1 to 5 each: readability at a glance; information accuracy (no fake numbers); visual hierarchy; colour (several accents, comfortable contrast, not harsh); polish (rounded, consistent spacing, aligned); motion quality (meaningful, smooth, calm when idle); asset use (real robot heads, badges and icons fit the style); phone layout; performance (idle CPU under 3 percent, 60 fps on interaction, 30 fps ambient); reduced-motion behaviour; glitch adds energy without hurting readability. Then the process: each iteration the builder takes Playwright screenshots at 1440 px desktop and 390 px phone plus a 5-second recording of the motion, an INDEPENDENT grader (a separate review call by a different model or session than the builder, given only the screenshots, the recording frames and the rubric, never the builder reasoning) scores every item with a one-line reason, the lowest scores are fixed, repeat until every item is 4 or better, at most 5 rounds per pass, every round keeps its screenshots and a scores.json and scores.md in docs/design/review/STAGE/roundN/, the final screenshots and the score table go to the owner. Requirements, in order (write acceptance for each): R-066 Command Center views read one shared data layer with real labelled numbers only (every displayed number has a label and a hover explanation; a number that cannot be shown accurately is hidden; the board accuracy tests from S4 extend to the new views). R-067 Everything Swarm Watch has today stays: current views move under a Classic tab, every existing route and page still renders (a test requests each). R-068 The Hive overview: a central brain entity, one node per project around it (status colour, percent done, tickets building, needs-you count, machine), a top stat strip (projects, agents live, tickets done today, needs you) with real numbers only, a legend by category (building, blocked, needs you, done) with consistent colours, bottom panels (live event log in plain words, lanes and who is working, what the swarm saved (relays avoided, retries, time), a throughput chart). R-069 Particle streams flow from each project node into the core: density equals active agents, speed equals tickets per hour, drawn on canvas at 30 fps, paused when the tab is hidden. R-070 The brain entity is an original animated design and the masterpiece asset of the board: it breathes with total activity, glows with the lane colours in use, pulses on a merge, flickers amber on a failure, rests when idle, and shows one still frame under reduced motion. R-071 Clicking a project zooms smoothly into the Project Cockpit and a breadcrumb returns to the Hive; both views have deep links and keyboard access. R-072 The Project Cockpit: the orchestrator as an animated character built on the robot heads style showing its real state (thinking, dispatching, waiting on you, reviewing); stages and waves as rings; tickets as nodes moving ready, building, review, done, each building ticket showing the head of its lane. R-073 Cockpit sides and bottom: ticket lists (building, ready, blocked, done) with search; a live run stream (what each worker is doing, progress, pace and ETA, PRs and deploy status). R-074 The real robot heads (tools/watch-assets/robot-*.js) are used everywhere an agent appears, with lane colours and live states (working, thinking, sleeping, error, idle) exactly as on the All Projects page; Kenney bubbles and Fluent badges sit on top; no stand-in drawings. R-075 Signature glitch style with PowerGlitch: glitch-in on first load and on Hive to Cockpit switches, brain flickers on event bursts and a stronger one on failures, a light glitch on hover of project names, ticket ids and robot heads, a brief glitch as numbers update with CountUp, one glitch on a new needs-you chip then still, stronger red or amber glitch on failures and rate limits, a glitch reveal of section headings on scroll into view; rules: each burst under 400 ms, never a continuous loop, never on text being read during an update, at most 3 glitches at once on screen, all off with prefers-reduced-motion; a test checks the limits. R-076 A command palette (Cmd-K or Ctrl-K) jumps to any project, ticket, run, PR, doc or command, with keyboard navigation and recent items. R-077 A first-visit guided tour (skippable, replayable from the help menu) explains the Hive, the Cockpit, the colours and the palette in plain language. R-078 A Resources and Tools hub: searchable docs, runbooks, every swarm command with a copy button, links to repos, PRs and deploys, lane setup guides, and the asset library with licences; plugin-style: a new tool or resource is added by dropping a JSON or Markdown entry into a folder, with no code change, validated by a schema test. R-079 The phone layout: the Hive becomes a vertical stack, the Cockpit becomes tabs; no horizontal scroll at 390 px; touch targets at least 44 px. R-080 Performance, accessibility and review: idle CPU under 3 percent, ambient canvas at 30 fps, pause when hidden, full reduced-motion support (still frames), keyboard access and contrast 4.5 to 1 for text; every stage passes the self-review loop (score table at 4 of 5 or better on every item from docs/design/review-rubric.md, at most 5 rounds, rounds kept in docs/design/review/) and every new asset is licence-checked, vendored with VENDOR.json and listed in docs/third-party.md. Stages CC1 to CC5 in the design doc: CC1 foundations (shared data layer, Classic tab move, glitch kit and rules, performance harness, Playwright review tooling and the rubric, real robot head mounting helper); CC2 The Hive (brain entity, ring of projects, streams, stat strip, legend, bottom panels); CC3 Project Cockpit (orchestrator character, rings, ticket nodes, lists, run stream); CC4 Experience (command palette, tour, Resources and Tools hub, phone layout, deep links, zoom transition); CC5 polish pass (glitch signature across the board, review loop final rounds, performance budget check). Each stage has a gate that includes the review score table. Two existing tests read the real roadmap (tests/build-progress-roadmap.test.mjs and tests/build-progress-ledgers.test.mjs): run them after the edit; update only the fixed requirement count or stage list expectation (65 requirements becomes 80, stages gains S10) with a comment, never loosen anything else. Run swarm scope check docs/scope/roadmap.md if possible: every requirement needs a heading and an Acceptance list. No secrets, no real hosts.
jobs.ignoreTestsReason: tests that reference these files in passing are covered by the full suite run before merge
